_note: Canned responses for offline mode. Quotes in `fallacies` must appear word-for-word in oracle.DEMO_PITCH or the verifier discards them.

personas.name: Dana Reyes
personas.background: solo maintainer of a logging library, 11 years in ops tooling
personas.quote: A focus group that talks back is a nice trick. I have been promised 'real objections' by three vendor decks this year and got a wall of green checkmarks.
personas.mind_change: Show me a transcript where the panel told you not to ship.

personas.name: Priya Nandakumar
personas.background: indie hacker, ships one small tool a quarter
personas.quote: If it runs in one command and does not ask me for an API key I do not have, I will try it on the next launch.
personas.mind_change: A single command with no account step.

personas.name: Marcus Webb
personas.background: platform engineer, reviews tools for a 400-person org
personas.quote: Synthetic personas are not research. If this is sold to a product team as validation, it becomes a liability the first time someone quotes it in a board deck.
personas.mind_change: An explicit label in every export that says synthetic, plus a doc note that it is not research.

dissent.objection: The product's central promise is unfalsifiable as presented: a synthetic panel cannot demonstrate real objections because the candidates are generated, not sampled, so a flattering result is indistinguishable from a working one.
dissent.what_would_change_it: A published run where the panel returns KILL and a named objection survives a blind review by 5 outside maintainers.

civil.positioning: Reads as a critique tool for people who distrust their own market research, not as a replacement for it. The local, no-account posture is the differentiator.
risks: Synthetic output gets quoted as research by someone who skipped the label
Local-only distribution limits discovery to people already in the terminal
opportunities: Publish adversarial transcripts rather than testimonials
Seed-based reproducibility lets two people compare runs

personas.name: Hal Brennan
personas.background: runs growth for a competing research tool
personas.quote: I can clone the page in a weekend and charge for the hosted version. The only thing I cannot clone is the part you have not shipped.
personas.mind_change: A distribution channel I cannot buy my way into.

personas.name: Dr. Ilse Farkas
personas.background: methodologist, reviews survey instruments for a research institute
personas.quote: "Real objection" is doing no work here. Real to whom, measured how, against what sampling frame? You cannot audit a claim whose terms are undefined.
personas.mind_change: A definition of 'real' with a threshold and a test that fails when it is not met.

personas.name: Owen Pike
personas.background: writes for a developer newsletter that thrives on teardown posts
personas.quote: For the piece I would need it to fail publicly. Give me a run where it tells you your idea is bad and you ship it anyway, and I will write it up.
personas.mind_change: A documented case where the tool was wrong and someone caught it.

dissent.objection: The pitch protects itself from measurement: 'real objection' is undefined, so any output can be defended as meeting it, and 'no account required' adds nothing falsifiable to compensate.
dissent.what_would_change_it: A stated threshold, e.g. 8 of 10 blind reviewers rate the objection as specific to the artifact, with the scoring sheet published.

fallacies.why: 'Real' has no threshold, so no output can ever fail the requirement.
It borrows 'focus group' while discarding sampling, which is the only thing that makes a focus group evidence.
Convenience is offered as a virtue in place of any claim about output quality.

cannibal.positioning: Reads as an argument-against-yourself tool. The hostile panel is the product; the pretty page is packaging.
risks: Hostile panels read as abusive rather than rigorous if the framing is off
Verified quotes are only as good as the artifact text those personas were given
opportunities: Ship the fallacy ledger as an export a team can argue over
Cannibal mode is the postable artifact: screenshots of your own pitch being dismantled
